messages:
Micah: Heads-up — enabling the new variant-chooser/kernel-selector in the runtime bumped p50 ~12% on the apples-to-apples replay harness when batch_size=1 + KV caching enabled. Repro steps below. :eyes:
Micah: Repro command:
```
./harness/replay --model rwd-7b-v1 --prompts replay_set_v2.json --decode-params 'temp=0.0,top_p=0.95' --kv-cache on --batch-size 1 --kernel-selector enabled
```
Anya: Can you paste the profiler flame or the short perf summary? curious where the extra time is (launch? memcpy? compute?)
Micah: Perf summary (aggregated across 1k requests): p50=48ms (was 43ms), p95=110ms (was 102ms). Kernel selector chose matmul_v2 for ~78% of steps; baseline used matmul_v1. Quick log snippet:
```
[kernel_selector] seq_len=32 chosen=matmul_v2 est_cost=0.62 actual_compute=0.58 mem_copy=0.07
[kv_cache] prefix_copy_bytes=12.3KB copy_count=1
```
Jamie: My gut — matmul_v2 has a slightly better flop profile for long sequences but higher kernel launch overhead / requires extra staging buffer for small seqs. With batch=1 that launch + staging wins vanish.
Lee: Were the decoding params and tokenizer the same between runs? stop-seqs? tokenizers can change token counts and shift seq distribution.
Micah: Yes confirmed: same prompts, same tokenizer (tokenizer_sync=true in harness), same stop sequences. This is apples-to-apples. I also re-ran with larger batch sizes and impact reduces (batch=8 p50 delta ~2%).
Anya: Try forcing kernel selector to fallback to matmul_v1 (force flag) and run the same harness. If p50 returns, we isolate selector decision as root cause. Example:
```
RUNTIME_KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_v1 ./harness/replay ...
```
Micah: Forced matmul_v1 run: p50=44ms, p95=105ms — basically baseline. So selector decision + small-batch path looks like the culprit.
perf-bot: [auto-summary] Experiment 1768412345: variant-chooser enabled -> p50 +12% at batch=1; forced fallback to matmul_v1 restores baseline. Logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/1768412345
Jamie: Hypothesis: cost model inside selector uses estimated compute only, but doesn't account for memcpy/staging + kernel-launch latency at small batch/seq. We should add a small-seq bias or measure kernel launch tail.
Micah: Plan: 1) run micro-bench of both kernels across seq_len {8,16,32,64,128} and batch {1,2,4,8}, capture (launch_ms, memcpy_ms, compute_ms). 2) instrument the selector to expose the estimated cost components in logs. 3) run replay harness with selector logging.
Lee: Also look into KV cache path: the log shows prefix_copy_bytes=12.3KB and copy_count=1 — is that an extra copy per request from selector path? Could be a buggy buffer normalization when selector picks matmul_v2.
Anya: I can add memcopy counters to tracing: increment mem_copy_count and bytes in the buffer_manager tracepoint. Will push a small diff to eng-runtime/tracing today.
Micah: Great. If we can reproduce reliably we'll do a quick canary that pins the older kernel for Hosted/Dedicated while we tune the selector. I'll open an RFC/bug and link the experiment.
Jamie: thumbs up. After microbench we can tweak selector cost heuristic: add fixed kernel_launch_penalty and per-copy penalty. That should reduce false positives for small batches.
Micah: Thanks — I'll post microbench results here once I have numbers. For now tagging this thread with :investigate: and adding to perf board.
Anya: quick note — include tokenizer token-length histogram in microbench outputs; selector decisions change a lot with a 1-2 token shift.
Micah: Will do. :thumbsup:
